name: Ehi
overview: Ehi is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as a son of Benjamin. He appears in the biblical record as one of the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt during the patriarchal period. Ehi is also associated with the Ahiramites, a group named after him under the alternative name Ahiram.
namesAndTitles: The name Ehi means 'my brother [is exalted],' reflecting a familial or relational exaltation. He is also called Ahiram, which carries a similar meaning, '[my] brother is exalted.' These names emphasize a theme of brotherly honor or elevation within his family or tribe.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ehi as a son of Benjamin. An inferred paternal relationship links him to Hushim, suggesting Hushim as his father. Beyond these connections, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ehi's significance lies primarily in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational lineage that would later form the nation of Israel. His identification with the Ahiramites highlights a tribal or familial subgroup within Benjamin. Through these associations, Ehi contributes to the genealogical and tribal structure that underpins the biblical narrative of God's covenant people.
